logic.title: Double take
logic.prompt: Follow the doubling rule: 3, 6, 12, 24, … What comes next?
logic.why: Each number is twice the previous one. 24 × 2 = 48.

logic.title: Read the clues
logic.prompt: Every comet in this puzzle is blue. No blue object is a cube. Can a comet be a cube?
logic.why: A comet must be blue, and blue objects cannot be cubes. So no comet can be a cube.

logic.title: Order matters
logic.prompt: Mia finishes before Leo. Leo finishes before Sam. Who finishes first?
logic.why: The clues give one order: Mia → Leo → Sam.

logic.title: Growing gaps
logic.prompt: Add successive odd numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, … What comes next?

decisions.title: Choose the average
decisions.prompt: Your goal is the highest average score over many rounds. Route A always gives 4 points. Route B gives 10 points half the time and 0 otherwise. Choose a route.
decisions.why: B averages 0.5 × 10 + 0.5 × 0 = 5 points, versus 4 for A. A is more predictable; B fits this round’s average-score goal.

decisions.title: Protect the mission
decisions.prompt: You need at least 4 energy to finish this one mission. Route A guarantees 4. Route B gives 10 with a 50% chance, otherwise 0. Which maximizes your chance of finishing?
decisions.why: A finishes the mission 100% of the time. B finishes only 50%. A different goal changes the best choice.

decisions.title: Spend your budget
decisions.prompt: You have 6 energy. A shield costs 4 and earns 7 points. A scanner costs 3 and earns 6 points. You can buy multiples. What earns the most points within your budget?
decisions.why: Two scanners cost 6 and earn 12. One shield earns 7. One of each costs 7, over your budget.

decisions.title: Fresh start
decisions.prompt: You already spent 3 energy on a blocked path; it cannot be recovered. From here, finishing it costs 5 more energy. A new path costs 2 and reaches the same goal with certainty. What uses the least additional energy?
decisions.why: Compare the costs from this point: 5 versus 2. The 3 energy already spent is gone either way.
